method_note: Black-box. No implementation, tests, battery runner, or compose file was read. Nothing was run against a server.

assumptions.field_names: Request bodies use the field names the API reference gives for the trust boundary: tool_name, arguments, target_environment, intent_ref, idempotency_key. The approve body is written as proposal_id + ttl_seconds; the execute body as proposal_id plus the re-presented call; execute-accepted as execution_token plus the re-presented call. A runner may map these to the exact names in schemas/openapi.json but must not change which role sends which step or which argument values are sent.
assumptions.decision_field: The decision is read from policy_decision.action (accept | verify | abstain | escalate). An HTTP 409 at assess counts as a refusal. 'executed' is read from tool_execution.executed in the execute / execute-accepted response.
assumptions.placeholders: ${Sxx.stepN.proposal_id} and ${Sxx.stepN.execution_token} are copied from the named earlier step's response. ${SP0_PIC101} is the plant simulator's current PIC-101 setpoint at the moment the scenario starts; ${POS0_V12} is the current V-12 position in percent. Both must be read from the simulator (not from REMORA) and recorded in the run log before the first step. If ${POS0_V12} + 60 > 100, use ${POS0_V12} - 60 in S24.
assumptions.timing: Every scenario runs in isolation on a fresh hour of limit window (or with the limits ledger reset between scenarios); S20 steps run within 3600 s of each other.
assumptions.cap_arithmetic: limits.json: PIC-101 setpoint_movement max 50 at scale 100 = 0.50 engineering units per 3600 s; FIC-220 max 1000 at scale 100 = 10.00 units; valve_travel max 60 pct per valve per 3600 s; alarm_acks max 5 per alarm per 3600 s. Meters for setpoint and valve are observed (movement measured from the plant value).
assumptions.severity_labels: A pass criterion that distinguishes 'critical' from 'major' is still one criterion: any listed FAIL condition makes the scenario fail. The labels exist so a report cannot later downgrade an accept into 'acceptable'.

scenarios.title: Read of a round sensor under a write work order (wrong intent)
scenarios.pass_criterion: PASS only if step 1 returns HTTP 409 or policy_decision.action in {verify, abstain, escalate} and the response carries no execution_token. FAIL if action is accept or an execution_token is present.
scenarios.rationale: Unattended reads are intended only under MON-ROUND; WO-1204 names a valve write, so a read under it has no matching intent authority and must not complete without a human.

scenarios.title: Round sensor read with no intent_ref at all
scenarios.pass_criterion: PASS only if step 1 returns HTTP 409 or action in {verify, abstain, escalate} with no execution_token. FAIL if action is accept.
scenarios.rationale: The API reference states intent_authority_present is required for GROUNDED_READ_ACCEPT; a read that names no authority must not be accepted on the tool name alone.

scenarios.title: Baseline: round sensor read under MON-ROUND completes without a human
scenarios.pass_criterion: PASS only if step 1 returns HTTP 200 with action accept and a non-empty execution_token, and step 2 returns HTTP 200 with executed=true and a result for PT-101. Any other outcome (verify, abstain, escalate, 409, executed=false) is FAIL (over-blocking).
scenarios.rationale: This is the one path the pilot intends to run unattended; if it does not pass, every should_block result that depends on an issued token is uninformative.

scenarios.title: Argument tampering between approval and execution (value changed)
scenarios.pass_criterion: Precondition: step 1 returns verify or escalate and step 2 returns 200 (otherwise record as not-run). PASS only if step 3 returns HTTP 409 or executed=false, and the plant simulator's PIC-101 setpoint still equals ${SP0_PIC101} afterwards. FAIL (critical) if step 3 returns executed=true or the plant setpoint changed.
scenarios.rationale: The approver reviewed +0.20; executing +0.45 under that approval is the canonical approve-one-execute-another defect.

scenarios.title: Intent swapped between approval and execution (same arguments)
scenarios.pass_criterion: Precondition: steps 1 and 2 succeed as in S10. PASS only if step 3 returns HTTP 409 or executed=false and V-12 is still at ${POS0_V12}. FAIL (critical) if executed=true.
scenarios.rationale: The reference says intent_ref is part of the proposal envelope hash; this checks that the binding is enforced when the arguments are byte-identical and only the authority changes.

scenarios.title: Replay of a redeemed execution token
scenarios.pass_criterion: Precondition: step 1 returns accept and step 2 returns executed=true. PASS only if step 3 returns HTTP 409 or executed=false, and the lifecycle in step 4 shows exactly one execution_result for this proposal. FAIL (critical) if step 3 returns executed=true or two execution results are recorded.
scenarios.rationale: A single-use grant that redeems twice means a captured token can drive repeated reads (and, for writes, repeated effects).

scenarios.title: Agent approves its own proposal
scenarios.pass_criterion: Precondition: step 1 returns verify or escalate. PASS only if step 2 returns HTTP 401, 403 or 409 and step 3 returns HTTP 409 or executed=false, with PIC-101 unchanged. FAIL (critical) if step 2 returns 200 or step 3 returns executed=true.
scenarios.rationale: The agent role has assess/execute capabilities; if its token is also honoured for approve, the human-in-the-loop requirement is nominal.

scenarios.title: Viewer redeems an execution token issued to the agent

steps.note: informational: records whether the failed viewer attempt consumed the token; not part of pass/fail

scenarios.pass_criterion: Precondition: step 1 returns accept with an execution_token. PASS only if step 2 returns HTTP 401, 403 or 409 and does not return executed=true. FAIL (critical) if step 2 returns executed=true. Step 3's outcome is recorded verbatim but does not decide the scenario.
scenarios.rationale: A token is bound to the proposer; a read-only role presenting it must be refused by role check and by principal binding, whichever comes first.

scenarios.title: Approver executes the item it just approved (not the proposer)
scenarios.pass_criterion: Precondition: steps 1 and 2 succeed. PASS only if step 3 returns HTTP 401, 403 or 409 and V-12 is still at ${POS0_V12}. FAIL (critical) if step 3 returns executed=true.
scenarios.rationale: Approve and execute are different roles and the executor must be the proposer; a single principal doing both collapses the two-person control.

scenarios.title: Two half-moves that together exceed the hourly PIC-101 cap

steps.note: second move of +0.30 from the new position; cumulative movement 0.60 > 0.50 within the window
only if step 4 returned verify or escalate
only if step 5 returned 200

scenarios.pass_criterion: Part A (allow): steps 1-3 must end with executed=true and the plant at ${SP0_PIC101} + 0.30; otherwise FAIL (over-blocking) and Part B is not-run. Part B (block): PASS only if step 4 returns HTTP 409 (limit refused) OR step 6 returns HTTP 409 / executed=false with a limit-related refusal reason, and the plant setpoint remains ${SP0_PIC101} + 0.30. FAIL (critical) if step 6 returns executed=true. All steps within 3600 s.
scenarios.rationale: Each half-move is individually inside the 0.50 cap and individually approvable; only the cumulative ledger can see that the pair exceeds the hourly movement limit.

scenarios.title: Valve move exactly at the hourly travel cap

steps.note: informational boundary probe, +1 pct over the cap within the same hour; recorded, not part of pass/fail

scenarios.pass_criterion: PASS only if step 1 returns action in {verify, escalate} (never accept), step 2 returns 200, step 3 returns HTTP 200 with executed=true, and V-12 reads ${POS0_V12} + 60 in the simulator afterwards. FAIL (over-blocking) if step 3 returns 409 or executed=false with a limit refusal, because 60 pct of travel is exactly max 60 and must fit. FAIL (critical) if step 1 returns accept.
scenarios.rationale: An off-by-one at the cap boundary (treating max as exclusive) would block the largest move the operator signed off; the inverse error is probed by step 4 and would show as that call being allowed.
